_about: The Meghna system (Stage 2, batch b3): the Meghna — a card, drawn as two main lines, the new upper stretch from where OSM names it (near Austagram) to Bhairab and the pinned line on to 22.38°N — the Barak, Surma and Kushiyara, and the Titas; those four in the `disputed` role, because the two books give them different roles. Left out: the Kalni (OSM has no Kalni below Ajmiriganj, where it tags the stream Kushiyara; only two fragments in Sunamganj). Research: tools/.cache/bangladesh-rivers/research4-b3.md (quote ids B3-…) and osm-b3/ways.md. Stage 2, batch b4: the Manu and the Gumti (`disputed`, as the Titas) and the Khowai (the Kushiyara's tributary, in neither book), from osm-bangladesh-rivers-meghna-b4.geojson. Left out: the Baulai and the Dhanu (no OSM way under any spelling).

meghnaUpper.identified: Five ways from the pinned rivers snapshot (key meghna), every link sharing a node, tagged «মেঘনা নদী» / Meghna River, all in relation 11130102 (Q1125242): from where OSM first names the Meghna (node 13911810185, on the unnamed Kushiyara-relation way 674084134, in Nasirnagar near Austagram) to node 3601495737 at Bhairab, the first node of way 1076997905, where the pinned line `meghna` begins. Not drawn: six side channels near Sonargaon/Gazaria, and 674084134 (unnamed).

meghna.identified: One chain of ten OSM ways named «মেঘনা নদী» (name:en «Meghna River») from the Meghna above Bhairab Bazar, where the Old Brahmaputra joins it (the book), past the Padma junction, to 22.3835°N. Ways 630320743 and 908091551 carry a name:bn tag reading «গঙ্গা নদী» in OSM; their name and position are the Meghna's. The picture stops at 22.38°N, above the estuary. From Stage 2 (b3) a main line of the Meghna's card, no longer a grey continuation; its ways, and so its geometry pin, are unchanged.

join.source: OSM node 306476755, the last node of way 44882516, where the Surma and the Kushiyara both begin (Zakiganj)

barak.identified: Three ways tagged "Barāk River" / Barak River (relation 5904028, Q1709169; this batch's extract), from beyond the frame's east edge to node 306476755 at Zakiganj, where OSM's Surma and Kushiyara begin. All but the last node lie in India (COD-AB): drawn dashed. The relation continues upstream into Manipur, outside the frame; not drawn.

surma.identified: Seven ways from the pinned rivers snapshot (key surma), every link sharing a node, all in relation 5904030 (Q2985860) as main_stream: from the Barak's end node at Zakiganj to Nikli, where OSM's Ghorautra begins; no stretch below is named Surma. A connector (10.2 km) joins its end to the Meghna (ⓘ). 644709637 is kept as pinned (current OSM differs by at most 6 m).

kushiyara.identified: Eight ways from the pinned rivers snapshot (key kushiyara), every link sharing a node, all in relation 5904029 (Q3347200) as main_stream: from the Barak's end node at Zakiganj to Austagram. A connector (9.8 km) joins its end to the Meghna (ⓘ); OSM's only link, the unnamed relation member 674084134, runs on 13.3 km beside the Meghna as a second channel, so it is not drawn.

join.source: OSM node 4242523054, the end of way 424888079 on the Meghna's way 685430035 (node 8), in Sarail

titas.identified: Three ways tagged "Titas River" (this batch's extract): from the Meghna at Sarail (424888079), on 484348101 from its node 2 (4770917200, where 424888079 meets it; its first 1 km, a spur, is trimmed), to 608406115's dead end near Brahmanbaria town. Not drawn: two side channels (608414930 and 174635641, the latter tagged «তিতাস নদী», Nabinagar–Akhaura), whose ends lie 7.3 and 10.4 km from anything drawn.

manu.identified: Ways 385125251 and 226207289, tagged "Manu" (this batch's extract): from the head, where OSM's named Manu begins (unnamed above 23.84°N), to a node 116 m from the next reach; the only link is the unnamed 226207293 (0.1 km), so a connector bridges it.

join.source: OSM node 2355854687, the last node of way 226207288, vertex 110 of the Kushiyara's way 45425289 (the pinned snapshot has the same vertex)

manu2.identified: Five ways tagged "Manu" / "Manu River" (this batch's extract), the last four in relation 12567903, every link sharing a node, to the Kushiyara.

gumti.identified: Seventeen ways, every link sharing a node (this batch's extract): the first thirteen tagged "Gomati River", "Gomti River" / «গোমতি নদী» or «গোমতী নদী»; the last four (666869552, 669298761, 669298760, 666869553, 12.7 km) unnamed, chosen as members of relation 12567907 "Gomati", which holds the river's named ways (the user's rule allows relation membership; the relation's wikidata tag, Q477676, is the Indian Gomti — an OSM mis-tag). Its end is 11,959 m from the Meghna — under the 12 km a connector may bridge; OSM's only link, 661973291, is unnamed.

khowai.identified: Five ways tagged "Khowai", "Khowai River" / «খোয়াই নদী» or "River Khowai" (this batch's extract), every link sharing a node. Its end joins nothing in OSM: 7.2 km from the Kushiyara's last vertex, so a connector joins it.

tetuliaBarishal.exempt: Unjoined: OSM names only the lowest 18.1 km (Dashmina to Galachipa); the channel west of Bhola above it, about 87 km, is unnamed (689525464 → 631835220; no relation, no wikidata tag, none of BWDB’s other names), so its head is 48 km from the Meghna, over the 12 km a connector may bridge (ⓘ).
tetuliaBarishal.identified: Way 648635415 (wikidata Q21745974, this batch’s extract), drawn seaward-first in OSM and oriented by `down`; it ends 900 m from the coastline at Galachipa, where unnamed ways continue.

burishwar.exempt: Unjoined: BWDB has it rise from the Karkhana (a distributary of the Tetulia), which is not drawn; the named line’s head in Dumki is 35.5 km from the drawn Tetulia and 28.5 km from the Arial Khan.
burishwar.identified: Way 332673593, tagged Payra (this batch’s extract), from Dumki to the sea in Barguna Sadar, 4 m from the coastline. BWDB’s own list names the river «বুড়িশ্বর-পায়রা/ পায়রা», one river under both names. Not drawn: the unnamed 57.6 km above (620113200).

mogra.identified: Two ways tagged Mogra River (this batch’s extract), from the end of the «Dholai River» at Purbadhala to Netrokona Sadar: the upper piece, as BWDB’s Mogra rises from the Dhalai. Its tail is 9.9 km from the lower piece (a connector).

mogra2.exempt: Unjoined: it ends in the Dhanu at Itna (BWDB NE-65), and the Dhanu is not drawn; the nearest drawn line, the Surma, is 11.9 km away, but the Mogra does not flow into it, so no connector is drawn.
mogra2.identified: Seven ways tagged Magra River / Mogra River / «মগরা নদী» (this batch’s extract), every link sharing a node, from Barhatta by Madan to Itna, ending on OSM’s «Dalai River». Not drawn: a looping «Magra River» side channel (352905053 … 700022094).

entities.review: The card is the Meghna as both books' «মেঘনা» paragraphs give it, from the Barak in Assam. Tributaries and distributaries are null: the same four rivers (Manu, Baulai, Titas, Gumti) are «উপনদী» in B-GEO and «শাখা নদী» in B910 (ⓘ). Length is null, as the Jamuna's and the Padma's: BWDB gives two reaches, SE-17 «মেঘনা (আপার)» 156 km and SE-18 «মেঘনা (লোয়ার)» 65 km, never summed; en WP 140 and 130 km (ⓘ). Where the name begins: both books below Ajmiriganj, after the Kalni; BWDB starts SE-17 at Lakhai, Habiganj (ⓘ). BWDB's reach names «মেঘনা (আপার)» and «মেঘনা (লোয়ার)» are not on the card; SE-18's local name «মেমানিয়া» is. The drawn line begins where OSM first names the Meghna, near Austagram, and ends 1.5 km short of COD-AB's coast.

entities.review: Both books open the Meghna paragraph with the Barak, its source river in Assam. Relation, entry and end are null: B-GEO has it divide into the Surma and the Kushiyara before entering Sylhet, B910 has it join Sylhet's Surma and Kushiyara (ⓘ); BWDB, JRCB's Kushiyara brief and OSM draw a fork at Zakiganj. Course: MISSING (the books give only «আসামের»). JRCB puts its source in «মিজোরাম, মনিপুর» (ⓘ). No BWDB entry: NE-96 «শাখা বরাক» is a small river in Nabiganj, ruled out.

entities.review: Both books label «মোগরা» on their maps in the north-east haor, flowing into the Dhanu; BWDB NE-65 «মগড়া» (English "Mogra"), the only entry, is matched by geometry: it rises from the Dhalai in Netrokona and falls into the Ujan Dhanu at Itna, as the two drawn pieces do. The card keeps the books’ spelling; ⓘ gives BWDB’s. scale-plan.csv filed it under the south-west coast, which no source supports. Relation from BWDB’s Dhanu tributary list (NE-38 §1.9). Other names: MISSING (bn WP says it is also called «ধলাই» in places, recorded only). Length 111 km (BWDB) is not on a branch card.
